Trust all is well. We are in full preproduction of our "Radical Breakthroughs" series/season for Closer To Truth. 
We expect to finish preproduction, with a complete production plan (including contributors, locations and schedule), by 
mid/late November. 
Attached are phase-one (rough) outlines of the first two episodes. As the first phase of our preproduction, we 
will have similar 2-3 page outlines for all 13 episodes. No contributors/interviewees will have been contacted, nor on-
location filming schedules developed (needed for visual relevance and efficiencies). (At this stage - phase one of 
preproduction - we appreciate feedback on content, especially for those episodes covering topics you have thought 
about, like these on mathematics.) 
The second phase of preproduction begins when we commence contacting the potential 
contributors/interviewees, assessing their ideas, relevance and communication skills. We will develop, for each of the 13 
episodes, the narrative arc (for each episode) and simulate the sequences of contributors/interviewees and the flows 
and structure of arguments. We will also ask prospective contributors/interviewees for their suggestions of additional 
contributors/interviewees, which will all lead to a second document, with updated contributors/interviewees, for each 
episode. 
EFTA_R1_01807285

In the third phase of preproduction we will develop an on-location filming plan, optimizing locations for filming 
all 13 episodes in parallel (obviously), clustering in key areas (e.g., San Francisco, Oxford/Cambridge, etc.). We will also

contributors/interviewees). 
The nature of the process is that we are always and iteratively modifying, tweaking, improving the arc, outline 
and structure of episodes. 
Peter Getzels, producer/director of Closer To Truth, and I are truly excited about our "Radical Breakthroughs" 
series - nothing like it, anywhere! - and we appreciate your vision, generosity, confidence and trust.

contributors/interviewees, assessing their ideas, relevance and communication skills. We will develop, for each of the 13

episode. 
In the third phase of preproduction we will develop an on-location filming plan, optimizing locations for filming 
all 13 episodes in parallel (obviously), clustering in key areas (e.g., San Francisco, Oxford/Cambridge, etc.). We will also 
ask some contributors/interviewees to fly into these locations (as we cannot go to a city for only 2.3 
contributors/interviewees).

A few notes=from my last visit with a few pics attached: 
LSJ - Pool Cabana Au=io: 
The amplifiers are good quality and approp=iate for the application but there is no DSP (Digital Signal 
Processing) fo= the speakers. This means that every speaker, whether it's a low fr=quency subwoofer or a high 
frequency top speaker, is getting the full flat s=ectrum of sound. This will result in each speaker trying to deliver audio i= 
a range that it was not designed for and it will not sound as good as it c=n. 
The rece=ver that is being used was intended for a surround sound theatre room, not f=r a powerful 
stereo system. It has been configured as best as possible, but=it not intended for this application. 
<=div> 
To re-use the current amps, the solution is to add a DS= stereo pre-amp. We recommend a QSC 
processor like this: 
https://www.qsc.co=/systems/products/q-sys-platform/products-peripherals-accessories/q-sys-
cor=s/core-110f/ 
=ou can avoid using that processor if you buy amplifiers with a DSP built-in= Like this: 
https://www.k-array.com/en/products/type/a=plifiers/ <https://www.k-
array.com/en/prod=cts/type/amplifiers/> 
For=the audio source and control, rather than using an optical cable from the i=ac, I recommend using a 
control interface that would be installed in the ra=k. An example is a SONOS connect. This can be controlled over the
